data.hypothesis: Factoring the final permutation lookups into two reused z-offset table bases may reduce repeated index additions/address work across the eight scalar corner hashes. This changes hash addressing only; the compiler may already perform equivalent factoring, so compare against the selected hash-prefix-factored parent and retain the original baseline as the campaign anchor without presuming a speedup.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use the prefix-factored program as a promising measured parent, but measure any further hash-addressing changes independently.
memory_lessons.claim: The valid prefix-factored candidate measured 0.28947 s over three samples versus the baseline's 0.31093 s; this result belongs to that candidate and is not proof that further address factoring helps.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a distinct final-lookup addressing change against the selected parent while checking all correctness cases.

memory_lessons.applicability: Do not infer performance from smaller tables or lookup-based gradient selection; these alter different parts of the scalar path.
memory_lessons.claim: The table-width and selector-table candidates were valid but measured slower than the best prefix-factored result, so table representation and gradient selection remain independent hypotheses.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Continue isolating a single hash-addressing or gradient-selection change per experiment.

data.notes: The catalog reports four distinct measured programs and no repeats. Prior observations show the prefix-factored parent at 0.28947 s (valid) versus baseline at 0.31093 s (valid); the compact-entry and selector-table variants were also valid but slower than that best result. This candidate preserves the selected parent's prefix factoring and changes only the final z-offset addressing. It has not been measured; the controller should validate the fixed tolerance and all specified checks before comparing timing.
transformations: In Noise, create two const pointers to the permutation table at iz and iz+1, then use the existing pxy prefixes as indices for the eight final corner hashes.

Replace the repeated final lookup indices pxy + iz and pxy + iz + 1 with equivalent accesses through the two shared bases; leave gradient selection, interpolation, octave control flow, table contents, and pixel traversal unchanged.
